“What? You intend to go to school?”

“Yes. Is there a problem, Archer?”

“…Not precisely, but surely—”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What? You’re going to school?”
“Yes. Do you have a problem with that, Archer?”
“…No problems, it’s just…”

アーチャーは言いよどむけど反論はしない。
昨日一日で、遠坂凛という人間は一度決めた事を覆す性格ではない、と理解したからだろう。
口にしなくても判るというか、アーチャーは皮肉屋だけど妙に素直なところがあって、認めた事柄に文句をつける事はないみたいだ。

pages.en:
Archer falters, but offers no objection.

After spending yesterday with me, he has apparently grasped that Rin Tohsaka is not the sort of person to reverse a decision once she has made it.

Perhaps he can tell without my having to say it. Archer may be a cynic, but there is an oddly straightforward side to him: once he acknowledges something, he does not complain about it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Archer hesitates, but does not object.
He must have realized yesterday that I’m not the type to take back my decisions.
I can kind of tell without him saying so. Archer is sarcastic, but he has an honest side to him. So it seems he won’t complain about something he’s accepted.

pages.ja:
うむ、ようするに不器用な忠義者なのだ。

pages.en:
Yes. In short, he is loyal—just awkward about it.

That is less a reasoned conclusion than an intuition I arrived at after observing him yesterday.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Yes, in other words, he’s faithful in an awkward way.
This is my conclusion… no, more of an intuition after watching Archer for all of yesterday.

pages.ja: 「凛。マスターになったからには、常に敵マスターを警戒しなくてはならない。学校という場は、不意の襲撃に備えにくい場所だろう」

pages.en: “Rin. Now that you are a Master, you must remain constantly alert to enemy Masters. A school is hardly a place where one can prepare for a surprise attack.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Rin. As you are a Master now, you must always be cautious of other Masters. School is a place where it’s hard to remain prepared against sudden attacks.”

pages.ja: 「そんなことはないけどね。いいアーチャー？ わたしはマスターになったからって、今までの生活を変える気はないわ。それにマスター同士の戦いは人目を避けるモノでしょう？ それなら人目につく学校にいれば、不意打ちされる事はまずないと思うけど」
pages.jaRuby: 「そんなことはないけどね。いいアーチャー？ わたしはマスターになったからって、今までの生活を変える気はないわ。それにマスター同士の戦いは人目を避けるモノでしょう？ それなら人目につく学校にいれば、不意打ちされる事はまずないと思うけど」
pages.en: “Not necessarily. Listen, Archer. I have no intention of changing the life I've always led merely because I became a Master. Besides, battles between Masters are supposed to take place away from witnesses, aren't they? If I stay at school, in full view of other people, a surprise attack should be very unlikely.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “That’s not true. Look, Archer, even though I am a Master now, I don’t intend to change my lifestyle. Besides, a battle between Masters is something that should be done out of public view, right? So, if we are at school where there are lots of people, I don’t think we’ll see any kind of surprise attacks.”

pages.ja:
「……そうか。凛がそう決めたのなら私は従うだけだ。
だが、霊体化して君の護衛をするぐらいはいいのだろうな。まさか学校に行っている間はここに残れ、などとは言うまい」

“…I see. If that is your decision, Rin, I need only obey.

“But surely you will allow me to accompany you in spirit form and stand guard. You cannot mean to order me to remain here while you are at school.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I see. If that’s what you’ve decided, I can only obey.
But I can guard you in spirit form, right? You don’t intend for me to stay here while you go to school?”

「それを聞いて安心した。信頼に応えるのは騎士の勤め、せいぜい期待に添うとしよう」

“I am relieved to hear it. A knight's duty is to repay the trust placed in him. I shall endeavor to meet your expectations.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Of course not. Not just at school, but I will want you by my side whenever I go outside. It is the Servant’s role to protect the Master, so I’ll be counting on you.”
“I’m relieved to hear that. It is the duty of a knight to answer trust placed on us. I shall do my best to meet your expectations.”

“You mean, suppose there were a Master at school?”

“Precisely. Students and teachers may be the only people with easy access to the grounds, but would it not be troublesome if one of those already inside were a Master?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“But Rin, just hypothetically, what would you do if there were an enemy in that safe place?”
“Hm? What, are you suggesting there might be a Master at school?”
“That’s right. It’s certainly hard for anyone who isn’t a teacher or student to get in, but wouldn’t it be a problem if someone already there is a Master?”

“Honestly, if there is another family of magi besides mine, of course they would be the first people I investigated.

“How do you know there isn’t a Master?”
“Hey, it’s only natural to investigate another family of magi in the same town.
He isn’t a Master and his successor doesn’t have enough magical energy to become a Master, so we can just ignore them.”

pages.ja: 「そうか。つまり凛の通う学校には、もう一人魔術師がいるのだな。だがマスターになれるほどの魔力を持ち合わせていない、と？」

pages.mirrorMoon: “I see. So, there is another magus at the school you go to. But you say that magus doesn’t have sufficient magical energy to become a Master, is that correct?”

“…Well, for now, at least.

“I keep telling you, there isn't one. Magi are sensitive to the presence of their own kind. After sharing a school for a year, I would sense another mage no matter how thoroughly they hid themselves.

“I can state it categorically: there are only two magi at our school. One is me, and the other is an apprentice without enough power to become a Master.

“Do you understand? Your caution is completely misplaced. What you're describing simply cannot happen.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Like I said, there aren’t any. Magi are sensitive to other magi. If we were at the same school for a year, I should be able to sense other magi no matter how well they hide it.
I will state with confidence that there are only two magi at our school. One of them is me, and the other is only an apprentice who doesn’t have enough power to become a Master.
Do you understand? Your caution is just needless worrying. It’s completely impossible.”

“Fate has a way of making the impossible occur.

“I am asking only that, should such a thing happen, you refrain from taking your frustration out on me.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“That’s why this is only a hypothetical scenario. There’s always another side to things.
It’s only natural for unexpected things to occur.
I’m saying that when it does happen, do not blame me.”

pages.ja:

pages.en:
Archer lets out a dry little laugh.

…That attitude alone makes me want to take my frustration out on him, but if I rise to every barb, I'll be late for school.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Archer smiles dryly.
…Just that action makes me want to take it out on him, but if I did, I would be late for school.

pages.ja: 「そんな事あるわけないじゃない。もしもの話っていうのは、起きないからもしもの話なのよ。もしそんな事になったら、その時はわたしの見通しが甘かったってだけなんだから」
pages.jaRuby: 「そんな事あるわけないじゃない。もしもの話っていうのは、起きないからもしもの話なのよ。もしそんな事になったら、その時はわたしの見通しが甘かったってだけなんだから」
pages.en: “That's never going to happen. A hypothetical is a hypothetical because it doesn't happen. And if it somehow does, that will only mean I underestimated the situation.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “That won’t happen. A hypothetical is a hypothetical because it won’t happen. If it does, it just means my analysis was too shallow.”

「よし、確かに聞いたぞ。それでは行こうか凛。

“Good. I heard you quite clearly. Let us be off, Rin.

“Your school is thirty minutes away. If we do not leave soon, you will fail to arrive on time.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“All right, I’ll remember that. Let’s go then, Rin.
It should take thirty minutes to get to the school, so we won’t make it unless we leave soon.”

“I'm surprised. So hypotheticals really do happen.”

“Yes, I am surprised as well. It pays to find fault with everything. I never imagined the habit would prove useful.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I’m surprised. Hypotheticals do happen.”
“Yes, I am surprised as well. Wow, it pays to argue over everything. It had an unexpected payoff.”

pages.en:
We trade those barbs the moment we pass through the front gate.

Students are streaming toward their classrooms around us, and homeroom will begin at any moment.

Amid the tide of people racing one another toward the building, I stand there with Archer, frozen in dismay.
pages.mirrorMoon:
As soon as we pass the school’s main gate, we joke around like that.
Around us are students heading to classrooms and it’s almost time for homeroom.
In the crowd of people rushing into the school building, we stand dumbfounded.

If he’s doing this so openly, he must be a real big shot…”

“Whoever planted something this vile in my territory is getting beaten into the ground. No discussion.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Who knows? I don’t care if he’s third class or first class.

pages.en:
I snort and stride across the schoolyard.

As a mage, I have no intention of mouthing pretty platitudes. But whoever laid this bounded field will receive the punishment they deserve, or I will not be satisfied.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I walk angrily through the schoolyard.
As a magus, I’m not about to mince words, but I can’t be satisfied until I properly punish the creator of this boundary field.

本来人間の手におえぬ英霊をまるごと召喚し、あまつさえマスターに仕える使い魔に固定した。
そのデタラメさは、まさに聖杯が万能である事の証でもある。
pages.en:
But the Holy Grail made that impossibility real.

It summons Heroic Spirits whole—beings ordinarily beyond all human control—and fixes them in place as familiars who serve their Masters.

The sheer absurdity of the feat is itself proof of the Grail's omnipotence.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But the Holy Grail made that impossibility into reality.
It summons the heroic spirit, beyond human control, and turns it into a familiar obedient to the Master.
That nonsense is proof that the Holy Grail is almighty.

pages.ja:
そうして年代を問わず、近くは百年前、遠くは神代の頃から英霊は召喚された。
七人の英霊はそれぞれ七人のマスターに従い、おのがマスターを守護し、敵であるマスターを駆逐する。
……あらゆる年代、あらゆる国の英雄が現代に蘇り、覇を競い合う殺し合い。
それが、この儀式が聖杯戦争と呼ばれる由縁だろう。

pages.en:
Thus Heroic Spirits are summoned without regard to age—from as recently as a century ago, or as far back as the Age of Gods.

Seven Heroic Spirits obey seven Masters, each defending their own Master and eliminating the Masters who stand as enemies.

…A death match in which heroes of every land and every age return to the modern world and vie for supremacy.

That, surely, is why the ritual is called the Holy Grail War.
pages.mirrorMoon:
And with the passing of years ignored, the heroic spirits are summoned. The most recent from a hundred years ago, the oldest from the ancient days.
The seven heroic spirits obey each of the seven Masters, protect them, and eliminate the Masters of the enemy.
Heroes from every age and country are revived into the present day, to kill one another for supremacy.
That is why this ritual is called the Holy Grail War.

pages.ja:
……もっとも、聖杯にも限界があったらしい。
いかに聖杯といえど、精霊じみた連中を無差別に呼び出す事は出来なかった。
悪魔と呼ばれる第六架空要素の実体化には“人々が創造したカタチ”が必要なように、
英霊たちも、こちらの世界で活動できるカタチが必要なのだ。

pages.en:
…Even the Holy Grail appears to have its limits, however.

Omnipotent or not, it cannot summon these spirit-like beings indiscriminately.

Just as the materialization of the Sixth Imaginary Element—the beings called demons—requires a form conceived by humanity, Heroic Spirits require forms through which they can act in this world.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…But it seems the Holy Grail has its limits too.
Even the Holy Grail cannot indiscriminately call unto the spirit-like beings.
Just as a form invented by humans is required for the imaginary sixth element, known as the devil, to take form, the heroic spirits also need a form to live in this world.

pages.ja:
それが彼らの仮の名前であり、この世界に許された存在の在り方。
聖杯は英霊たちが形になりやすい“器”を設け、器に該当する英霊のみを召喚させる。
現代へのパスポートと言うか、予め使い魔としての役割を用意しておき、召喚された英霊がその役割に憑依する事で、仮初めの物質化を手助けする。

pages.en:
Those forms are their temporary names, the modes of existence permitted to them in this world.

The Grail prepares seven vessels, the classes in which Heroic Spirits may readily take shape, and summons only spirits compatible with one of them.

They are passports into the modern world: roles prepared in advance for familiars. By possessing those roles, the summoned Heroic Spirits are helped into temporary material form.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That form is their temporary name, and the way they exist in this world.
The Holy Grail has furnished “classes” so that the heroic spirits may take form more easily, and it only summons the heroic spirits that match these classes.
It’s like a passport to the present as it sets up a role as a familiar in advance. By allowing the summoned heroic spirit to take on that role, it helps the spirit to take form.

pages.en: As there are seven Masters chosen by the Grail, so there are seven Heroic Spirits to serve them.
pages.mirrorMoon: If there are seven Masters chosen by the Holy Grail, there are also seven Servants obeying those Masters.

剣の騎士、セイバー。
槍の騎士、ランサー。
弓の騎士、アーチャー。
騎乗兵、ライダー。
魔術師、キャスター。
暗殺者、アサシン。
狂戦士、バーサーカー。
この七つのクラスのいずれかの属性を持つ英霊だけが現代に召喚され、マスターに従う使い魔
サーヴァントとなる。

pages.en:
Seven classes are assigned in advance.

Saber, the knight of the sword.

Lancer, the knight of the spear.

Archer, the knight of the bow.

Rider, the mounted warrior.

Caster, the mage.

Assassin, the killer in the shadows.

Berserker, the mad warrior.

Only Heroic Spirits bearing the attributes of one of these seven classes can be summoned into the present and become Servants—familiars bound to obey a Master.
pages.mirrorMoon:
There are seven furnished classes.
Knight of the sword, Saber.
Knight of the lance, Lancer.
Knight of the bow, Archer.
Mounted soldier, Rider.
Magus, Caster.
Silent killer, Assassin.
Mad warrior, Berserker.
Only the heroic spirits with attributes of these classes are summoned to the present to obey the Masterand become a Servant.

That is the Servant system—

the summoning of and contract with Heroic Spirits, beings beyond human control, granted so that humans may contend for that equally unreachable miracle: the Holy Grail.

The ultimate contest, impossible in any other Holy Grail War, conducted on this land alone—!
pages.mirrorMoon:
That is the Servant System
A summoning and contract with a heroic spirit beyond human control, to win the “miracle” beyond human grasp.
The ultimate competition, held only on this ground, the one and the only Holy Grail War!

ランサーの技だ。
直線だけの打突から、一転してアーチャーの手首を払うなぎ払い。

pages.en:
“—!”

One clash rings louder than all the rest.

The short blade that parries Lancer's spear flies from Archer's hand.

It is Lancer's technique.

After an unbroken succession of linear thrusts, he changes without warning to a sweep aimed at Archer's wrist.

Archer sees the blow coming and still cannot evade it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“!”
A loud crash.
The shortsword that deflected Lancer’s lance flies from Archer’s hand.
This is Lancer’s technique.
A straight thrust that turns into a sweep at Archer’s wrist.
It was a blow Archer could not avoid even had he seen it coming.

強く弾けば弾いた以上の鋭さで斬り返され、かといって最小の力で受け流しても隙は一向に生まれない。

pages.en:
There is no sure way to receive a spear with a sword.

Strike it aside with force, and it returns with greater violence. Deflect it with the smallest possible movement, and still no opening appears.

In the end, a battle between sword and spear comes down to a single question: which fighter can kill the other from beyond the other's reach—
pages.mirrorMoon:
There is no effective way of parrying a lance with a sword.
A strong rebuff only results in a stronger counterattack, and a weak rebuff does not create any openings.
The important aspect of the battle between a sword and a lance lies in defeating the enemy when he is at the wrong range

アーチャーを追い詰めようと踏み込んでいた足が止まる。

“—Fool.”

Lancer's insult carries no hesitation.

The foot that had pressed relentlessly forward comes to a halt.

—He means to decide the battle in a single instant.

Lancer plants himself firmly upon the earth. His gaze meets that of the now-unarmed Archer.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Idiot.”
There’s no hesitation in Lancer.
His movement to push Archer back stops.
He must intend to end the match in a single instant.
The stares of the firmly placed Lancer and the swordless Archer clash.

In that instant—

Lancer's spear becomes a flash of light, loosed three times in the space of a single breath.

The eye cannot follow it.

The brow. The neck. The heart.

Three thrusts, every one aimed at a vital point—!

In that instant.
The lance is thrust just like a flash of light.
It can’t even be seen.
Forehead, neck, and heart.
Three shots are launched, any one a fatal blow!!

a pair of lights strikes back the flashes no eye can see…!

But.

Short swords have appeared once more in Archer's hands.

They resemble the earlier blade: Chinese weapons with the heavy shape of cleavers.

“Tch. Two swords…!”

Its speed rises higher still, announcing his intention to leave Archer alive no longer.

His hawk-like eyes say that he will not retreat anymoreno, that he will only advance from now on.

The clash of blades rings against my ears like a finely wrought piece of music.

Two voices of steel ring together.

The swordplay never ceases. Sparks fly as its rhythm builds without end.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The clashing sounds are like a well orchestrated music.
Two steels clanging against each other.
The sparking clashes increase in rhythm without pause.

The space in which they fight is nearly a vacuum.

Their battle drags the surrounding air into itself; draw near, and the pressure alone seems capable of slicing flesh to ribbons.

“…”

In truth, it lasts only an instant.

But to me, watching, it stretches so long that I cannot breathe.

The battle of the two is like a vacuum.
It sucks in the air around them, and it seems like anything approaching them would be cut to pieces.
“”
In reality, it only lasts an instant.
But for me looking on, it seems to take an infinitely long time.

Lancer fights to keep Archer from entering his guard.

Archer advances behind the shield of his twin blades.

Their exchange passes a hundred strikes, and again and again Archer loses his weapons.

Lancer tries not to let Archer near him, while Archer advances using his swords as a shield.
Over a hundred blows have been thrown, and Archer loses a sword every time.

But each loss lasts only an instant. In the next, fresh swords occupy Archer's hands, and every time they appear, Lancer yields another fraction of a step.

At last, Lancer acknowledges his mistake.

He does not know the identity of the man before him.

But if he continues to dismiss him as a bowman, he will be the one defeated.

But it’s only for a moment as Archer has a sword in his hand in the next instant, forcing Lancer back a little each time.
Lancer finally admits his carelessness.
That even though he doesn’t know who is before him, he will be the loser if he dismisses him as a mere bowman.

The distance opens.

Perhaps seeking to begin the contest anew, Lancer withdraws far beyond Archer's reach.

…His speed is monstrous.

Archer's charge defied reason, but even that was slow beside Lancer.

The movement with which Lancer slips out of range has all the speed and supple grace of a leopard.

The distance widens.
Probably to recover, Lancer puts a large distance between them.
…His speed is extraordinary.
Archer’s charge was out of this world, but it was still slow compared to Lancer.
The movement of his retreat had panther-like speed and agility.

“…Twenty-seven. I've knocked that many from your hands, and still you have more.”

Lancer mutters in irritation.

No. That is not irritation so much as bewilderment.

“…Twenty-seven. I’ve disarmed you that many times, yet you still have more.”

No, it’s more like confusion.

…I share it.

According to Father, a Servant bears only one weapon.

Each is charged with tremendous magical power. They are not things a Servant can produce one after another as Archer does.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I feel the same way.
According to Father, a Servant carries only one weapon.
Their weapon is filled with magical energy, so it’s not something that can be created one after another, like Archer was just doing.

pages.ja:

言いかえれば悪魔、天使の類に近い。

pages.en:
A Servant is a hero whose spiritual rank has been elevated after death to stand alongside elemental and holy spirits.

Put another way, they resemble beings such as demons or angels.

They are powerful familiars even without armament, but their greatest weapon is the “proof of the hero”: the magic item known as a Noble Phantasm.

Servants are heroes that sublimate their spirits after death, equaling the holy spirits.
To put it another way, they are like devils or angels.
They are powerful familiars on their own, but their most powerful weapon is their “proof of heroism”, a magical item called their “Noble Phantasm”.

それは宝具そのものが代えのきかない最終兵器だからでもある。

pages.en:
A Noble Phantasm is a weapon or piece of armor favored by the Servant while they lived as a hero. In the truest sense, it is their ace in the hole.

For any Servant, the Noble Phantasm is a unique and singular armament.

That is because the Phantasm itself is an irreplaceable final weapon.
pages.mirrorMoon:
A Noble Phantasm is a weapon or armor the Servant used when they were a hero, and it’s treated as a last resort.
The Noble Phantasm is the one and only weapon for a Servant.
This is because the Noble Phantasm is an ultimate weapon without equal.

pages.ja:
……ランサーの持っている槍だって、ランサーがその気になれば“宝具”としての能力を発揮するだろう。
宝具とはそれだけで優れた武器だけど、その本領は“真名”を以て力を解放させる事にある。

…The spear Lancer carries must reveal its powers as a Noble Phantasm if he chooses to unleash it.

A Noble Phantasm is an exceptional weapon in its own right. Its true function, however, is released through the invocation of its True Name.

…The lance that Lancer is using will show its power as a Noble Phantasm when Lancer deems it necessary.
A Noble Phantasm is an impressive weapon by itself, but its true ability is to release all its power using its “true name”.

These are the weapons of heroes who once slew dragons, killed gods, and ruled over all creation.

A Servant expends their own magical energy to activate a Noble Phantasm.

In that sense, it resembles magecraft.

Using the Phantasm as a catalyst, the Servant reproduces the legendary destruction attributed to it.

Heroes’ weapons which rule over all others, and which have killed dragons and gods.
Servants activate their Noble Phantasms using their magical energy.
It’s much like magic.
Servants recreate the destructions in legend using their Noble Phantasm as a catalyst.

pages.ja:
宝具は決して使い捨てにできる物ではない。
アーチャーが何十と持ち出した剣は、たしかにそれぞれが名剣のようだけど、アーチャーの“宝具”ではないのだろう。

A Noble Phantasm can never be treated as disposable.

He is an Archer-class Servant.

Therefore, the Noble Phantasm he conceals must be a bow.

He is the Servant Archer.
So the Noble Phantasm he conceals must be a bow.

pages.en:
“What is wrong, Lancer? It is unlike you to stand back and observe. Where has all that vigor gone?”

“…Tch. You old fox. Still running your mouth?”

“What’s wrong, Lancer? It’s not like you to just stand there and watch. Where’s the energy you had just now?”
“…You’re talking crap, you cheater.”

ランサーの苛立ちはもっともだ。
ランサーは槍兵として戦ったというのに、アーチャーは剣士として戦い、これを凌いだ。
いわばアーチャーとしての手の内をまったく見せていない状態である。

Lancer's irritation is entirely justified.

Lancer fought as a spearman. Archer met him as a swordsman and endured.

In other words, Archer has yet to reveal a single aspect of his power as an archer.

It is only natural that a deadly pressure should gather around Lancer.

Lancer’s irritation is understandable.
Even though Lancer fought as a spearman, Archer fended him off as a swordsman.
Which means, Archer hasn’t shown any of his abilities yet.
So it’s natural for Lancer to feel ghastly.

二刀使いの弓兵なぞ聞いた事がない」

pages.en:
“…Fine. I'll ask. What country's hero are you?

“I've never heard of a bowman who fights with two swords.”

“You, on the other hand, are easy to identify. They say only the swiftest heroes are chosen for the Lancer class, and you are foremost even among them.

“There cannot be three spearmen of your caliber in all the world. Add the agility of a beast, and only one likely name remains.”

I’ve never heard of a bowman using two swords.”

There aren’t three lancers in this world at your level. And on top of that, there’s only one with such beast-like agility.”

「

あまりの殺気に、呼吸を忘れた。

the force of his murderous intent makes me forget to breathe.

Crap.

I enter the house without announcing my return and flop onto the sofa.

Archer is not back yet.

I let out a hollow sigh and spend several minutes listening absently to the ticking clock.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I enter the house without saying anything and sit on the sofa.
Archer isn’t back yet.
I sigh and listen to the clock for a few minutes.

“After witnessing a battle like that, what am I doing sitting here in a daze?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Huh, I have to switch gears.
What am I doing, daydreaming after a battle like that?”

考えるべき事は山ほどある。
取り立てて重要なのはサーヴァントについて。
わたしはついさっき、知識でしか知らなかったサーヴァント同士の戦いを目の当たりにしたんだから。

pages.en:
I spring to my feet and make tea.

There are mountains of things to consider.

Foremost among them are the Servants.

Only moments ago, I witnessed with my own eyes a battle between beings I had known solely through study.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I jump up and brew some tea.
There are so many things to think about.
Most importantly, the Servants.
I have just witnessed a battle between Servants I had previously only understood intellectually.

pages.jaRuby: 「ランサーか……宝具を使われそうになった時は焦ったけど、実際使ってたら正体は判ったのよね……」
pages.en: “Lancer… I panicked when it looked as though he would use his Noble Phantasm, but if he actually had, I would have learned his identity…”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Lancer, huh…? I panicked when he almost used his Noble Phantasm, but I would have found out his identity if he had used it…”

敵サーヴァントを打倒するには、その正体を知ることが近道となる。
自分の正体さえ知らないバカものは例外として、サーヴァントにとって最大の弱点はその“本名”なのだ。
サーヴァントの本名
正体さえ知ってしまえば、その英霊が“どんな宝具を所有しているか”は大体推測できる為だ。

pages.en:
The surest path to defeating an enemy Servant is to discover who they are.

Leaving aside one particular idiot who does not even know his own identity, a Servant's greatest weakness is their “actual name.”

Once you know a Servant's name—their identity—you can generally deduce what Noble Phantasm that Heroic Spirit possesses.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The easiest way to beat an enemy Servant is to learn their identity.
Ignoring for the moment the idiot who doesn’t even know his own identity, the biggest weak point of a Servant is their “true name”.
Discovering the Servant’s true name… in other words, figuring out their identity… should let you take a guess at what kind of Noble Phantasm they might have.

pages.ja:
言うまでもないが、サーヴァントは英霊である以上、確固たる伝説を持っている。
それを紐解いてしまえば、能力の大部分を解明する事ができる。
サーヴァントがクラス名で呼ばれるのは、要するに“真名”を隠す為なのだ。
なにしろ有名な英雄ほど、隠し持つ武器や弱点が知れ渡っているんだから。

pages.en:
It should go without saying that every Servant, being a Heroic Spirit, possesses a firmly established legend.

Unravel that legend, and most of their abilities can be laid bare.

Servants address one another by class name for precisely this reason: to conceal their True Names.

The more celebrated the hero, the more widely known their hidden weapons and fatal weaknesses.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It goes without saying, but since Servants are heroic spirits, they have a legend associated with them.
If you figure out their legend, you should be able to find out most of their abilities.
Servants are called by their class names because they want to hide their true names.
Because the more famous a hero is, the more people know about their weapons and their weaknesses.

pages.ja:
サーヴァントとなった英霊は決して自分の正体を明かさない。
サーヴァントの正体を知るのはそのサーヴァントのマスターのみ。
マスターは自分のサーヴァントの正体を隠しつつ、他のサーヴァントの正体を探らなければならない、なんていう暗黙の了解があるほどだ。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
A Heroic Spirit summoned as a Servant never reveals their identity.

Only that Servant's Master knows who they truly are.

There is even an unspoken law: a Master must conceal the identity of their own Servant while seeking out the identities of all the rest.
pages.mirrorMoon:
A heroic spirit that becomes a Servant never gives out their true identity.
The only ones that know the Servants’ identities are the Masters.
There’s even a tacit understanding that the Masters hide their Servants’ identities while trying to discover the identities of the others.

pages.ja:
……聖杯戦争も今回で五回目。
各サーヴァントの優劣は、もちろん呼び出された英霊の格で決まる。
有名な英雄、伝説上優れた武装を持つ英雄ほど強力なのは言うまでもない。
pages.jaRuby:
……聖杯戦争も今回で五回目。
各サーヴァントの優劣は、もちろん呼び出された英霊の格で決まる。
有名な英雄、伝説上優れた武装を持つ英雄ほど強力なのは言うまでもない。
pages.en:
…This is the fifth Holy Grail War.

The relative power of its Servants naturally depends on the stature of the Heroic Spirits summoned.

Famous heroes—and heroes who possess outstanding legendary armaments—are powerful as a matter of course.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…This is the fifth Holy Grail War.
The qualities of the Servants are determined by the ranks of the summoned heroic spirits.
It goes without saying that the more famous heroes and the heroes with better weapons are stronger.

pages.ja:
もっとも、そういった英霊を召喚するのは難しい。
英霊召喚には、彼らが生前所有していた武装か、なんらかの縁がなければ召喚できない。
英雄の持ち物なんて、魔術協会でも数えるほどしか保有していないのだ。
だから大抵はわたしのように、数ある英霊の中から自分に合った英霊を召喚する事になる。

pages.en:
But summoning such a spirit is difficult.

To summon a Heroic Spirit, one requires either an armament the hero possessed in life or some other connection to them.

Even the Mage's Association owns only a handful of authentic heroic relics.

Most Masters, then, must do as I did: summon from among the countless Heroic Spirits the one most compatible with themselves.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But it’s difficult to summon such heroic spirits.
To summon a heroic spirit, one must have a connection with them such as a weapon they used during their lives.
Even the Magic Association has few of such things.
So generally, one will summon a heroic spirit that suits them, like I did.

pages.ja:
サーヴァントの強さは英霊の格で決まる。
が、事はそう簡単にはいかず、どんなに優れた英霊でも与えられたクラスによっては苦戦を強いられる。
それがクラス別の特殊能力、小が大を打ち倒す可能性だ。
pages.jaRuby:
サーヴァントの強さは英霊の格で決まる。

それがクラス別の特殊能力、小が大を打ち倒す可能性だ。
pages.en:
A Servant's strength depends upon the stature of the Heroic Spirit.

But matters are not so simple. Even a peerless Heroic Spirit may struggle if summoned into an ill-suited class.

That is the significance of each class's special ability: the possibility that the small may bring down the great.
pages.mirrorMoon:
A Servant’s strength is determined by the rank of the heroic spirit.
But it’s not that simple as even the most powerful heroic spirits may have a hard time depending on the class they are assigned to.
That is because of the special abilities assigned to each class, the possibility of the weak defeating the strong.

pages.ja:
七つのクラスはそれぞれ異なる付加能力を持ち、その相性によっては格上の相手に勝利する事もある。
その例で言えば、過去四回、知名度の低い英雄が大英雄をうち負かした事もあるらしい。
わたしが知りうる限り、最も優れたサーヴァントはセイバーだ。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Each of the seven classes receives a different additional ability. Depending upon how those abilities interact, a Servant may defeat an opponent of far greater stature.

Indeed, in the previous four wars, obscure heroes are said to have defeated heroes of the highest order.

As far as I know, the finest Servant class is Saber.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The seven classes each have a different additional ability, and one even has a chance of defeating an opponent of higher rank depending on the ability’s affinity.
To take an example, an infamous hero has defeated a great hero four times in the past.
As far as I know, the most powerful Servant is Saber.

セイバー、ランサー、アーチャーの三クラスは強力な対魔力を持つという。
率直に言って、この連中に魔術は通用しづらい。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
In each of the previous four wars, the Saber-class Servant survived to the very end.

The three knight classes—Saber, Lancer, and Archer—are all said to possess powerful Magic Resistance.

Put bluntly, magecraft has difficulty affecting any of them.
pages.mirrorMoon:
In all the previous four wars, Saber has made it to the final fight.
It is said that the three classes Saber, Lancer and Archer have strong magic resistance.
To put it simply, magic is pretty much useless against them.

pages.ja:
なにしろ神話の時代、魔法が当たり前のように跋扈していた世界で戦い抜いた戦士たちだ。
現代の魔術師が使う魔術など、彼らに触れただけで霧散するだろう。
……まあ、そういった訳でこの三つのクラスは基本にして優秀、と評されている。
pages.jaRuby:

They are warriors who fought through the Age of Myth, in a world where Magic ran rampant as a matter of course.

The magecraft employed by a modern mage might disperse the instant it touched them.

…For that reason, the three knight classes are considered both fundamental and exceptionally strong.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s because they are fighters who fought through the age of myths, when magics were used widely.
Magics that magi use now would probably dissipate just by touching them.
…Anyways, that’s why these three classes are considered the basics and the best.

pages.ja:
それ以外に注意すべきはバーサーカーのサーヴァント。
このクラスになって呼び出された英霊は、正気を失う。
文字通りマスターの操り人形となって活動する狂戦士となるのだが、その恩恵は生前の能力を大きく上回る“強化”だ。

pages.en:
The other class demanding particular caution is Berserker.

A Heroic Spirit summoned into this class loses their sanity.

They become a mad warrior who acts, quite literally, as the Master's puppet. In exchange, they receive an “enhancement” that raises their power far beyond what they possessed in life.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Another that’s worthy of mention is the Servant Berserker.
The heroic spirit summoned into this class loses their sanity.
Just as the name implies, they become a mad warrior puppet of their Master. The benefit from this is a “strengthening” of their power, far exceeding the powers they had when alive.

pages.ja:
もっとも、サーヴァントが強くなればなるほど、マスターにかかる負担は大きい。
過去、バーサーカーを得たマスターは暴走するサーヴァントを御する事ができず、魔力切れで自滅してきた。
ただ一人の例外もなく。

pages.en:
Naturally, the more powerful the Servant becomes, the greater the burden borne by the Master.

In previous wars, every Master who obtained a Berserker failed to control the rampaging Servant and destroyed themselves through depletion of their magical energy.

Without a single exception.
pages.mirrorMoon:
However, the more powerful a Servant becomes, the greater the burden it imposes on the Master.
In the past, Masters who summoned Berserker couldn’t control their rampaging Servants, and destroyed themselves by running out of magical energy.
No exceptions.

pages.ja:
聖杯戦争の勝敗を決めるのは、十中八九呼び出したサーヴァントの能力である。
そりゃあマスターの努力次第でいくらでも勝ち残る術はあるだろうけど、基本はサーヴァントによる潰し合いだ。

—Nine times out of ten, the outcome of the Holy Grail War is decided by the abilities of the Servant one summons.

Certainly, a Master's efforts can create any number of paths to survival. But fundamentally, the war is a contest in which the Servants destroy one another.

That is why a Master must exercise the utmost care when summoning a Servant—but—
pages.mirrorMoon:
The winners and losers of the Holy Grail War are largely determined by the abilities of the Servants.
Well, I expect there are ways to win it by the Master’s efforts, but it is basically a fight between the Servants.
That is why a Master should be very careful when summoning a Servant…

By the time I finish, the clock reads eleven—and of course I have already corrected it—and Archer returns.
pages.mirrorMoon:

I silently consider the plans we should make from now on.
The clock, fixed already, strikes eleven while I do so… and Archer comes home.

pages.ja:

pages.en:
“Welcome back. What did you find?”

“…Forgive me. I failed. His Master must be exceedingly cautious. At the very least, Lancer's Master was not based on this side of the city.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Welcome back. How did it go?”
“…I’m sorry. I failed. It must be one cautious Master. At the very least, Lancer’s Master is not on this side of town.”

pages.ja:
やっぱりそうか。
ランサーは一人きりだったし、ランサーのマスターは直接戦いの場に顔を出すタイプではなさそうだ。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Just as I thought.

Lancer fought alone, and his Master does not appear to be the sort who shows himself on the battlefield.
pages.mirrorMoon:
As I expected.
Lancer was alone and it seems his Master isn’t the type to show up for battles personally.

pages.ja:

そう、すべて思い通りに行くなんて事はない。
だから仕方ない。
今夜の事は授業料と思って諦めよう。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“I see. Well, it was never going to be that easy.”

No. Things cannot always proceed exactly as I wish.

There is nothing to be done.

I'll write tonight off as tuition.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. Well, I guess it won’t be easy.”
Yes, there’s no way everything will go as I might hope.
So it can’t be helped.
Let’s consider what happened tonight as a tuition fee for the lessons learned.

pages.ja: 「覇気がないなマスター。いつもの威勢はどうした。まさか先の一戦で怖じ気付いた、というのはなしだぞ。君が命じるのなら、今すぐにでもランサーとの再戦に赴いてもいい」
pages.jaRuby: 「覇気がないなマスター。いつもの威勢はどうした。まさか先の一戦で怖じ気付いた、というのはなしだぞ。君が命じるのなら、今すぐにでもランサーとの再戦に[ruby text=おもむ]赴いてもいい」
pages.en: “You seem dispirited, Master. What became of your usual vigor? Do not tell me that last battle frightened you. Give the command, and I am prepared to seek an immediate rematch with Lancer.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “You seem down, Master. Where are your high spirits? Don’t tell me you got scared by that one fight. If you so order, I am ready to go battle Lancer again right now.”

pages.ja:
いや、むしろそうするべきだろう
なんて無言で抗議するアーチャー。

わたし、落ち込んでいるように見えるのか。
pages.jaRuby:

わたし、落ち込んでいるように見えるのか。
pages.en:
Indeed, his silent protest says, that is what we ought to do.

…I see.

Do I look dejected to him?
pages.mirrorMoon:
Archer protests silently that we should do so.
…I see.
I guess I look depressed.

pages.en:
“Of course not. I'm holding back for one reason: I don't intend to waste my effort.”

“Hm? You do not wish to waste your effort…?”

“All seven Masters still haven't assembled. Tonight was unavoidable, but I won't fight again until the signal that formally opens the war. Father told me those were the rules of the Holy Grail War.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Of course not. I’m staying in only because I don’t want to do anything pointless.”
“Hm? Anything pointless…?”
“Well, all the Masters aren’t present yet, right? Tonight couldn’t be helped, but I wouldn’t start fighting before we get the signal. My father told me this is one of the rules of the Holy Grail War.”

pages.ja:

なるほど、と納得するアーチャー。
と。

pages.en:
“…I see. Your father was a Master as well.”

Archer nods in understanding.

—Then his expression grows grave, and he lapses into thought.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I see, so your father was also a Master.”
Archer nods, understanding.
Then.
Archer makes a troubled face and starts to ponder something.

pages.en:
He saw us. It will be dangerous unless I alter his memory.

More importantly, Lancer placed the elimination of a witness above his battle with us.

Lancer's judgment must reflect his Master's.

And if Lancer's Master is prepared to go that far, what will they do when the person they supposedly killed turns out not to have died?
pages.mirrorMoon:
He saw us, so it’ll be dangerous unless we adjust his memory.
Basically, Lancer prioritized eliminating the witness over his battle with us.
Lancer’s thinking probably matches his Master’s.
So… if such a Master finds out the guy they killed didn’t die, what would he do?

そんなヤツ、生かしておかない
」
ソファーから立ち上がる。
……あれから三時間。
間に合わないかもしれないけど、
あれだけのコトをして助けたんだから、間に合わない訳にはいかないじゃない
！

pages.en:
“—They won't let him live—”

I spring from the sofa.

…Three hours have passed.

It may already be too late.

But after everything I sacrificed to save him, I refuse to let it be too late…!

“He wouldn’t let the guy keep on living”
I get up from my sofa.
…It’s been three hours since then.
I might not make it, but…
After all I did, I have to make it on time!

幸い、アイツの家は知っていた。
いや、わたしが調べたわけじゃなくて、たまたま知り合いがよく遊びに行く家だっただけで、今まで一度も行った事はない。

Fortunately, I know where he lives.

Archer shows no enthusiasm.

He disapproved when I saved the boy Lancer nearly killed, and he disapproves of my going to save him again now.

雲に覆われた夜空の下、わたしたちは武家屋敷に辿り着いた。

pages.en:
—Midnight.

Beneath a cloud-shrouded sky, we arrive at a samurai residence.

The house stands at the edge of the residential district, nearly in the outskirts, and there is not a soul in sight.

Few homes stand nearby. If something were to happen, there would be no one to come running.

“—”

My breath clouds white.

The wind has risen.

It must be fierce above the rooftops; the clouds stream past with a roar.

Though Fuyuki's winters are supposed to be mild, the wind shivers along my spine, and my whole body shudders.

The supposedly warm wind of Fuyuki sends chills down my spine, making me tremble.

あまりにも冷たい大気に耳を澄ませる。
全てが凍気に支配された感覚で、確かに、敵の気配を感じ取った。

The air lies still, frozen solid.

I listen into the bitter cold.

The sensation is of a world ruled entirely by frost—and within it, unmistakably, I feel the presence of an enemy.

The presence comes from beyond this wall.

Lancer has already slipped inside. He is waiting to kill that boy a second time when he returns home, ignorant of everything.

“Who can say? But this makes seven. At last, all the pieces are assembled, Rin.”

Archer answers calmly.

My own judgment has abandoned me.

That is why I fail even to consider the next development, though it should be easy to foresee.

That is my error.

The battle is decided in an opening shorter than one second.

To me it is only a second.

To that Servant, it is an unforgivable eternity.

“!”

But I couldn’t react.
That was my mistake.
The battle ended with that small opening, not lasting even a second.
It might have been only a second for me, but for that Servant, it was an opening that couldn’t be ignored.

The Servant cuts him down.

Archer, who so magnificently weathered Lancer's ferocious assault, is felled by a single blow—

The condensed spell of wind could erase one or two houses without leaving a trace. It is one of ten jewels I have woven a little at a time, without missing a day in all my seventeen years.

If I expend it entirely, then even if I cannot defeat this Servant, I should at least be able to hold them back—

…But I cannot.

There is nothing to understand.

The swarm of winds, capable of tearing anything it engulfs to shreds in an instant, vanishes like a conjurer's trick the moment it touches the Servant.

—What overwhelming Magic Resistance.

The magical energy of a mere mage cannot put so much as a scratch on this Servant…!?

pages.en:
“—Ah.”

The wind blows.

The moon appears through a rent in the clouds, at the center of a spiral sky.

Moonlight pours down upon a face of impossible loveliness.

This is the Servant who sent Lancer fleeing,

defeated my Archer in a single blow,

and dispelled my magecraft as though it were nothing.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Wha…”
The wind blows.
In between the dark clouds in the spiral sky, the moon shines.
The falling moonlight and the beautiful face…
This is the Servant that drove off Lancer,
defeated my Archer in one strike,
and annulled my magic with no trouble.

“…”

Still resigned to death, I gaze at the moon.

I feel no urge to beg for my life, and there is no opening through which I might escape.

I will die here. Rin Tohsaka's Holy Grail War will end on its third day.

There is only humiliation and regret in that fate. I will vanish hating the enemy who killed me.

“”
I look up at the moon, accepting my death.
There’s no time for me to flee or plead for my life.
I will die here and Tohsaka Rin’s Holy Grail War will end on the third day.
There is only disgrace and regret, and I will probably vanish bearing a grudge against my enemy.

Death will come with the next blink, and still I find myself captivated again.

If anything frustrates me, it is that.

Even though I’m going to be killed in an instant, I adore her again.
That’s right.
If you ask for regrets, that’s it.
